test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: ​Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct option is: **3) with.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct preposition to use with **"correlated"** is** "with."**
 
• The phrase **"correlated with"** is commonly used to indicate that two things are related or associated with each other.
 
• In this case, high blood pressure is correlated with high sodium intake, meaning there is a relationship between the two.

The correct sentence is:* "A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be **correlated with**__ high sodium intake."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Why the other options are incorrect:

 
• **Option 1: "in" –** The preposition "in" is typically used to indicate location or a condition, but it is not used with "correlated" in this context. "In" would not correctly show the relationship between high blood pressure and sodium intake.
 
• **Option 2: "of" –** "Of" is generally used to show possession or association, but it does not fit with the verb "correlated" in this context. We don’t say something is "correlated of" something else.
 
• **Option 4: "for" – **The preposition "for" is used to indicate purpose or intention, but it is not used in the expression "correlated for." This would be grammatically incorrect in this context.
